intent: Build and validate the shell equivalent of the Python ast identity check, and record the deployment triage of all 29 over-cap shell scripts, so the splits that follow can be verified rather than assumed.
scope: docs/shell-split-verification.md - the harness usage, its self-test contract, and the triage table
Non-goal: any split; this commit only builds the tooling
changes: verify_shell_split.sh extracts each top-level function from a git rev and from the post-split files, normalises through shfmt -mn, and compares a hash per function. shfmt is already a REQUIRED_TOOLS binary here, so this adds no dependency.
It names the function that changed rather than reporting a whole-file diff, so a failure points at the seam.
Documented the triage: deploy.sh copies a hardcoded per-file list into /data/local/tmp/focus_mode and never deploys lib/, which decides the seam shape for 8 of the 29 scripts.

verification.evidence: IDENTICAL: all 5 top-level functions moved verbatim.

verification.command: verify_shell_split.sh against a copy with blank lines inserted every 7th line
verification.evidence: IDENTICAL - formatting changes do not register, which is what makes the check usable after shfmt and pre-commit autofixes.

verification.command: verify_shell_split.sh against a copy with one character of logic changed (file_path="$1" -> "$2")
verification.evidence: DIFFERENCE FOUND, naming process_packages and printing both hashes, exit 1. The first attempt at this test used sed 's/exit 1/exit 2/' on a file containing no 'exit 1' and reported IDENTICAL; diffing the mutation showed it had never applied. The harness was fine, the test was vacuous - which is exactly the failure mode a normalizer self-test exists to catch, and it is now written down.
Clean. An SC2329 on the cleanup function was fixed by inlining it into the trap rather than suppressing the warning.

verification.command: grep triage over all 29 over-cap shell scripts for cp/install/ln into deployed locations
verification.evidence: 13 scripts have a deployed copy: the 8 phone_focus_mode scripts (individually listed in deploy.sh), install_leechblock.sh and block_compulsive_opening.sh (preferred from /usr/local by pacman_wrapper.sh on every pacman call), and three that install helpers to /usr/local. The other 16 are safe to give an entry+lib shape. Confirmed the phone scripts source only config.sh, which is on deploy.sh's copy list - so a sibling-file seam works there but an entry+lib seam would not.
136 lines, under the 250-line cap. prettier runs on pre-push, so markdown is formatted before it can fail there.

risks: The function extractor is a brace-counting awk pass, so a function whose body contains an unbalanced brace inside a string or heredoc could be mis-delimited. Mitigated by the control test on a real repo script and by the harness reporting the function count, which would drop visibly if extraction went wrong.

The check covers top-level functions only. Code outside any function - the argument parsing and main flow most of these scripts end with - is not compared, so a split must still be verified by running the script.
rollback: git revert the commit; the harness and the documentation section disappear together.
Nothing depends on them yet, so no follow-up validation is needed after rollback.
